result.title: Task Vector Descent: Learning from Non-IID Batches
result.summary: A central challenge in continual learning is to acquire new knowledge without forgetting what the model has already learned. This challenge appears in language model training when training data comes from various domain-, user-, or task-specific distributions that are encountered unevenly over time. In such settings, successive minibatches are temporally clustered by distribution instead of being sampled i.i.d. from the overall data mixture. Training on temporally clustered data induces a stability-plasticity tradeoff. Adapting the model to the active distribution can improve the model on the active distribution but may lead to a performance degradation on data it previously trained on. We find that this tradeoff intensifies with longer exposure to the same distribution. We therefore ask if the parameter displacement produced by such a sequence (the task vector) should be fully retained or applied partially. We compare applying the full displacement ($λ=1$) with partial integration, which scales the task vector by $λ$ before applying it to the continuing model and scales the optimizer state by the same coefficient. Across continual pretraining, pretraining from random initialization, supervised post-training, and reinforcement post-training, we find that intermediate values of $λ$ often improve average continuing-model performance relative to full integration, particularly after longer same-distribution sequences. In continual-pretraining experiments with both controlled streams and naturally defined adaptation sequences, task-vector scaling outperforms full integration at the matched learning rate, showing that its benefits are not reproduced by learning-rate scaling alone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究非 IID、分布随时间聚类的持续学习场景下的稳定性—可塑性权衡，比较将任务向量（参数位移）完整保留（λ=1）还是按 λ 部分整合，并在持续预训练、从头预训练、监督与强化后训练中验证中间 λ 常优于全量整合。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线的具体线索在于「部分整合/缩放状态更新」这一机制：任务向量缩放与优化器状态同比缩放，可能可供核查 latent 推理状态更新幅度、轨迹训练中的贡献分配与信息坍缩问题，但其对象是参数空间而非视觉推理状态。
